sentences_text: Intel's 2024Q2 revenue was $12.83 billion, up 0.9% from 2024Q1 and down 0.9% from 2023Q2, while net results swung to a loss of $1.61 billion from a loss of $381 million in 2024Q1 and net income of $1.48 billion in 2023Q2.
Revenue of $12.83 billion compares with $12.72 billion in 2024Q1 and $12.95 billion in 2023Q2.
Gross profit fell 12.8% sequentially to $4.55 billion from $5.22 billion even as revenue edged up, so gross margin contracted 5.6 percentage points to 35.4% from 41.0%.
Year over year, gross profit declined 2.0% against a 0.9% revenue decline, so gross margin was down 0.4 percentage points from 35.8% in 2023Q2.

R&D expense was $4.24 billion, down from $4.38 billion in 2024Q1 but up from $4.08 billion in 2023Q2, putting R&D at 33.0% of revenue, down 1.4 percentage points sequentially and up 1.5 percentage points year over year.
SG&A expense was $1.33 billion, down from $1.56 billion in 2024Q1 and $1.37 billion in 2023Q2.

The reported operating loss widened to $1.96 billion from $1.07 billion in 2024Q1 and $1.02 billion in 2023Q2, taking operating margin to negative 15.3%, down 6.9 percentage points sequentially and 7.5 percentage points year over year.
Net margin was negative 12.5%, down 9.6 percentage points from 2024Q1 and 24.0 percentage points from 2023Q2.
Intel's 35.4% gross margin sat below the sector median of 45.8% but above the 25th percentile of 33.6%, and only one of the nine listed peers (MU, at 26.9%) reported a lower gross margin.
Intel's operating margin of negative 15.3% was below the sector 25th percentile of negative 7.9% and below all nine listed peers, against a sector median of 4.4%.

R&D at 33.0% of revenue was above the sector 75th percentile of 28.2% and the median of 19.5%, and Intel's 0.9% year-over-year revenue decline placed it among five companies with falling revenue alongside four of the nine listed peers (ON, TXN, ADI and MRVL).

The anomaly log flags a scale error on operating income for 2024Q1 and 2024Q2 that was not auto-corrected, so the operating income and operating margin figures above should be verified against the filed statements before use.
As a related check, the reported 2024Q2 operating loss is larger than gross profit less R&D and SG&A alone, which implies other operating items or a data issue that the analyst should reconcile.
Stockholders' equity is flagged as not comparable across 2023Q2, 2024Q1 and 2024Q2 due to a concept change and is excluded from this commentary.

Intel's 2024Q3 revenue rose 3.5% from the prior quarter to $13.28 billion but fell 6.2% from the year-ago quarter, while gross margin compressed to 15.0% and the company reported a net loss of $16.64 billion.
Revenue of $13.28 billion compares with $12.83 billion in 2024Q2 and $14.16 billion in 2023Q3.
Cost of revenue rose to $11.29 billion from $8.29 billion in 2024Q2, outpacing the 3.5% revenue increase, so gross profit fell 56.1% quarter over quarter to $2.0 billion.

Gross margin fell to 15.0% from 35.4% in 2024Q2, down 20.4 percentage points, and from 42.5% a year earlier, down 27.5 percentage points, as gross profit fell 66.8% year over year against a 6.2% revenue decline.

R&D expense was $4.05 billion, down from $4.24 billion in 2024Q2 but above $3.87 billion in 2023Q3, putting R&D at 30.5% of revenue, down 2.6 percentage points quarter over quarter and up 3.1 percentage points year over year.
SG&A expense was $1.38 billion, compared with $1.33 billion in 2024Q2 and $1.34 billion in 2023Q3.

Operating loss was $9.06 billion, an operating margin of negative 68.2%, a loss substantially larger than gross profit less R&D and SG&A, which implies other operating charges not itemized in the fact sheet.

Net loss widened to $16.64 billion from a net loss of $1.61 billion in 2024Q2 and net income of $297 million in 2023Q3, taking net margin to negative 125.3%, down 112.7 percentage points quarter over quarter and 127.4 percentage points year over year.
Intel's 15.0% gross margin sits below the sector 25th percentile of 24.5% and the sector median of 46.8%, and below all nine listed peers, the lowest of which was Marvell at 23.0%.

Intel's operating margin of negative 68.2% is well below the sector 25th percentile of negative 16.6% and the sector median of 5.0%, and below Marvell's negative 46.4%, the only negative operating margin among the nine peers.
Intel's net margin of negative 125.3% is far below the sector 25th percentile of negative 14.5%, while its R&D intensity of 30.5% exceeds the sector 75th percentile of 27.0%.

Three of the nine peers also reported year-over-year revenue declines, and Intel's 6.2% decline was smaller than those at Texas Instruments (8.4%), Analog Devices (10.1%) and ON Semiconductor (19.2%).

The anomaly log flags a scale error, not auto-corrected, in operating income for both 2023Q3 and 2024Q2, so this draft does not present prior-period operating income, operating margin changes or operating income growth rates until those figures are verified against the filings.
Stockholders' equity for 2023Q3 and 2024Q2 is flagged as not comparable due to a concept change; it is not used in this commentary.

Intel's 2024Q4 revenue was $14.26 billion, up 7.3% from 2024Q3 but down 7.4% from 2023Q4; operating income returned to a positive $412 million, while the quarter still closed with a net loss of $126 million.
All 2024Q4 and 2023Q4 company figures in this commentary were derived by the pipeline from annual and year-to-date filings rather than disclosed directly as quarterly amounts.
Revenue rose from $13.28 billion in 2024Q3 to $14.26 billion in 2024Q4, but remained below the $15.41 billion reported in 2023Q4.
Gross profit rose 179.6% quarter over quarter to $5.58 billion from $2.00 billion, far outpacing revenue growth, so gross margin expanded 24.1 percentage points to 39.2% from 15.0%.

Year over year, cost of revenue rose to $8.68 billion from $8.36 billion even as revenue fell, so gross profit declined 20.8% from $7.05 billion and gross margin contracted 6.6 percentage points from 45.7%.
R&D expense was $3.88 billion in 2024Q4, down from $4.05 billion in 2024Q3 and $3.99 billion in 2023Q4.
R&D as a share of revenue fell 3.3 percentage points sequentially to 27.2% from 30.5%, but rose 1.3 percentage points from 25.9% a year earlier because revenue declined faster than R&D spending.
SG&A expense declined to $1.24 billion in 2024Q4 from $1.38 billion in 2024Q3 and $1.62 billion in 2023Q4.
Operating income of $412 million compared with an operating loss of $9.06 billion in 2024Q3, lifting operating margin 71.1 percentage points to 2.9%.
Against 2023Q4, operating income fell 84.1% from $2.585 billion and operating margin narrowed 13.9 percentage points from 16.8%.

The 2024Q4 net loss of $126 million, equal to 0.9% of revenue, compares with a net loss of $16.64 billion in 2024Q3 and net income of $2.67 billion in 2023Q4, when net margin was 17.3%; net margin was down 18.2 percentage points year over year.
Intel's 39.2% gross margin sat between the sector 25th percentile of 35.6% and the median of 46.5%, and was above only one of the nine named peers, MU at 38.4%.
Intel's 2.9% operating margin was below the sector median of 6.0% and below all nine named peers, the lowest of which was AMD at 11.4%.
Intel's R&D intensity of 27.2% was slightly above the sector 75th percentile of 27.1% and well above the median of 19.2%.
Three of the nine named peers also reported year-over-year revenue declines, ADI down 3.6%, TXN down 1.7% and ON down 14.6%, and only ON declined more steeply than Intel's 7.4%.

The anomaly log flags a concept change in 2023Q4 stockholders' equity as not comparable; equity is not used in this commentary, but any balance-sheet comparisons against 2023Q4 should be treated with caution.

Because the 2024Q4 and 2023Q4 quarterly values were derived by subtracting year-to-date from annual totals, any restatement or reclassification between filings could affect these derived quarters and should be checked against the filed statements.

Intel reported 2025Q1 revenue of $12.67 billion, down 11.2% from $14.26 billion in 2024Q4 and down 0.4% from $12.72 billion in 2024Q1; the 2024Q4 figures used throughout were derived by the pipeline from filings rather than disclosed directly.
The net loss widened to $821 million in 2025Q1 from $126 million in 2024Q4 (derived) and $381 million in 2024Q1.
Year over year revenue was essentially flat, so the quarter's movement is mainly a sequential decline from the derived 2024Q4 level.
Gross profit fell 16.3% sequentially to $4.67 billion from $5.58 billion, faster than the 11.2% revenue decline, so gross margin compressed 2.3 percentage points to 36.9% from 39.2%.

Year over year, gross profit fell 10.4% from $5.22 billion while revenue was nearly unchanged, as cost of revenue rose to $8.00 billion from $7.51 billion, taking gross margin down 4.1 percentage points from 41.0%.

R&D expense declined to $3.64 billion from $3.88 billion in 2024Q4 and $4.38 billion in 2024Q1, but because revenue fell faster sequentially, R&D intensity rose 1.6 percentage points to 28.7% of revenue while remaining 5.7 percentage points below the year-ago level.
SG&A expense fell to $1.18 billion from $1.24 billion in 2024Q4 and $1.56 billion in 2024Q1.

Operating results swung to a loss of $301 million from operating income of $412 million in 2024Q4 (derived), with operating margin down 5.3 percentage points to negative 2.4% from positive 2.9%, as lower operating expenses did not offset the decline in gross profit.

Net margin was negative 6.5%, down 5.6 percentage points from negative 0.9% in 2024Q4 and down 3.5 percentage points from negative 3.0% in 2024Q1, and the net loss exceeded the operating loss in the quarter.
Intel's 36.9% gross margin sat below the sector median of 43.4% but above the 25th percentile of 31.5%, and exceeded only two of the nine listed peers, MU at 36.8% and ON at 20.3%.

Operating margin of negative 2.4% was below the sector median of 3.0% but above the 25th percentile of negative 9.9%, and among the nine listed peers only ON, at negative 39.7%, posted a lower operating margin.

Eight of the nine listed peers grew revenue year over year, with ON the exception at a decline of 22.4%, while Intel's R&D intensity of 28.7% exceeded the sector 75th percentile of 25.6% and the median of 19.3%.

The 2024Q1 operating income figure was flagged for a possible scale error that was not auto-corrected, so year-over-year operating income and operating margin comparisons are omitted here pending verification.

A 2024Q1 concept change in stockholders' equity was flagged as not comparable; equity is not discussed in this commentary, and all 2024Q4 values are pipeline-derived from annual less nine-month filings.
AMD reported 2024Q2 revenue of $5,835 million, up 6.6% from 2024Q1 and up 8.9% from 2023Q2, while operating income rose to $269 million from $36 million in the prior quarter.
Revenue increased from $5,473 million in 2024Q1 and $5,359 million in 2023Q2, while cost of revenue rose more modestly to $2,971 million from $2,913 million in the prior quarter.
Gross profit reached $2,864 million, up 11.9% quarter over quarter and 17.2% year over year, growing faster than revenue in both comparisons.
As a result, gross margin expanded to 49.1% from 46.8% in 2024Q1 and 45.6% in 2023Q2, up 2.3 percentage points sequentially and 3.5 percentage points year over year.

R&D expense rose to $1,583 million from $1,525 million in 2024Q1 and $1,443 million in 2023Q2, but because it grew more slowly than revenue sequentially, R&D intensity fell 0.7 percentage points to 27.1%, while remaining 0.2 percentage points above the year-ago level.
SG&A expense was $650 million in 2024Q2, compared with $607 million in 2024Q1 and $547 million in 2023Q2.
Operating margin improved to 4.6% from 0.7% in 2024Q1, up 4.0 percentage points sequentially and 5.0 percentage points from 2023Q2, when AMD recorded an operating loss of $20 million.

Net income was $265 million, up 115.4% from $123 million in 2024Q1 and up from $27 million in 2023Q2, lifting net margin to 4.5%, an increase of 2.3 percentage points sequentially and 4.0 percentage points year over year.
AMD's 49.1% gross margin sat between the sector median of 45.8% and the 75th percentile of 55.3%, and five of the nine named peers reported a higher gross margin.
AMD's 4.6% operating margin was slightly above the sector median of 4.4%, and its 4.5% net margin matched the sector median of 4.5%.
R&D intensity of 27.1% was well above the sector median of 19.5% but below the 75th percentile of 28.2%.
AMD's 8.9% year-over-year revenue growth trailed four of the nine named peers, including NVDA at 122.4% and MU at 81.5%, while five peers grew more slowly or declined.

The anomaly log flags a restatement or recast of 2024Q1 SG&A expense with both values retained, so the sequential SG&A comparison of $650 million against $607 million should be confirmed against the version the analyst intends to use.
Year-over-year percent changes in operating income are not presented because the 2023Q2 base was an operating loss, which makes the percentage not meaningful.
AMD reported 2024Q3 revenue of $6.82 billion, up 16.9% from 2024Q2 and up 17.6% from 2023Q3, while operating income rose to $724 million and net income to $771 million.
Revenue increased from $5.84 billion in 2024Q2 and $5.80 billion in 2023Q3 to $6.82 billion in 2024Q3.
Gross profit reached $3.42 billion, up 19.4% quarter over quarter and 24.5% year over year, growing faster than revenue on both comparisons.
As a result, gross margin expanded to 50.1%, up 1.1 percentage points from 2024Q2 and 2.8 percentage points from 2023Q3.

R&D expense rose to $1.64 billion from $1.58 billion in 2024Q2 and $1.51 billion in 2023Q3, but grew more slowly than revenue, so R&D as a share of revenue fell to 24.0%, down 3.1 percentage points quarter over quarter and 2.0 percentage points year over year.
SG&A expense was $721 million in 2024Q3, compared with $650 million in 2024Q2 and $576 million in 2023Q3, subject to the data caveat noted below.

Operating income of $724 million was up 169.1% from 2024Q2 and 223.2% from 2023Q3, lifting operating margin to 10.6%, an increase of 6.0 percentage points quarter over quarter and 6.8 percentage points year over year.
Net income of $771 million rose 190.9% from 2024Q2 and 157.9% from 2023Q3, and net margin reached 11.3%, up 6.8 percentage points quarter over quarter and 6.2 percentage points year over year.
AMD's 2024Q3 gross margin of 50.1% sat above the sector median of 46.8% but below the 75th percentile of 55.4%.
Operating margin of 10.6% was above the sector median of 5.0% but below the 75th percentile of 19.6%, while net margin of 11.3% compared with a sector median of 1.6% and a 75th percentile of 14.7%.
R&D intensity of 24.0% remained above the sector median of 20.2%.

AMD's year-over-year revenue growth of 17.6% was exceeded by four of the nine listed peers (QCOM, AVGO, MU and NVDA), while four peers (TXN, ADI, ON and INTC) reported year-over-year revenue declines.
The 2024Q3 SG&A figure was flagged in the pipeline's year-to-date consistency check as a suspect derivation, so the SG&A amount and its comparisons should be verified against the filing before use.

AMD reported 2024Q4 revenue of $7.66 billion, up 12.3% from 2024Q3 and up 24.2% from 2023Q4, with operating income of $871 million but net income down to $482 million; all 2024Q4 dollar figures were derived by the pipeline (full year minus nine-month year-to-date) rather than disclosed directly.
Revenue rose from $6.82 billion in 2024Q3 and $6.17 billion in 2023Q4 to $7.66 billion in 2024Q4.
Gross profit of $3.88 billion grew 13.5% quarter over quarter, faster than the 12.3% revenue increase, so gross margin expanded 0.6 percentage points to 50.7%.
Year over year, gross profit grew 33.4% against 24.2% revenue growth, lifting gross margin 3.5 percentage points from 47.2% in 2023Q4.

R&D expense was $1.71 billion in 2024Q4, and because revenue grew faster, R&D as a share of revenue fell to 22.4%, down 1.6 percentage points quarter over quarter and 2.1 percentage points year over year.
SG&A expense was $792 million in 2024Q4, compared with $721 million in 2024Q3 and $644 million in 2023Q4, though the 2024Q3 figure is flagged in the anomaly log.

Operating income rose 20.3% from $724 million in 2024Q3 and 154.7% from $342 million in 2023Q4, taking operating margin to 11.4%, up 0.8 percentage points sequentially and 5.8 percentage points year over year.

In contrast, net income fell 37.5% from $771 million in 2024Q3 and 27.7% from $667 million in 2023Q4, so net margin dropped to 6.3%, down 5.0 percentage points sequentially and 4.5 percentage points year over year, indicating items below operating income moved against the operating improvement.
AMD's 50.7% gross margin sat above the sector median of 46.5% but below the 75th percentile of 54.7%, and five of the nine named peers reported higher gross margins.
Operating margin of 11.4% was above the sector median of 6.0% but below the 75th percentile of 21.7%, and eight of the nine named peers posted higher operating margins, with only INTC lower at 2.9%.
Net margin of 6.3% was slightly below the sector median of 6.5%, while R&D intensity of 22.4% remained above the sector median of 19.2%.
AMD's 24.2% year-over-year revenue growth trailed four of the nine named peers, including NVDA at 77.9% and MU at 84.3%, while four peers including INTC and ON reported revenue declines.

The anomaly log flags 2024Q3 SG&A expense for a year-to-date consistency issue with a suspect fourth-quarter derivation, so the derived 2024Q4 SG&A figure and any sequential SG&A comparison should be verified against the filings before use.
Because every 2024Q4 dollar value and ratio rests on pipeline derivations from annual and year-to-date filings, the headline figures should be reconciled to the 10-K before distribution.

AMD reported 2025Q1 revenue of $7.44 billion, up 35.9% from 2024Q1 but down 2.9% from 2024Q4. The 2024Q4 comparison uses a pipeline-derived quarterly figure, computed from filings rather than disclosed directly.
Operating income was $806 million, up from $36 million in 2024Q1 and down 7.5% from a pipeline-derived $871 million in 2024Q4.
Revenue rose from $5.47 billion in 2024Q1 and fell from a pipeline-derived $7.66 billion in 2024Q4.
Gross profit of $3.74 billion grew 45.9% year over year, faster than revenue. Gross margin therefore expanded 345 basis points, from 46.8% to 50.2%.
Sequentially, gross profit fell 3.8%, more than revenue did, so gross margin narrowed 46 basis points from 50.7% in 2024Q4.
R&D expense was $1.73 billion, compared with a pipeline-derived $1.71 billion in 2024Q4. With revenue lower, R&D as a share of revenue rose 88 basis points to 23.2%.
Year over year, R&D intensity fell 4.6 percentage points from 27.9%, because revenue grew faster than R&D spending.
SG&A expense was $886 million, up $94 million from a pipeline-derived $792 million in 2024Q4 and up $279 million from $607 million in 2024Q1.
Operating margin was 10.8%, up 10.2 percentage points from 0.7% a year earlier and down 54 basis points from 11.4% in 2024Q4.
Net income was $709 million, up 47.1% from a pipeline-derived $482 million in 2024Q4 and up 476.4% from $123 million in 2024Q1.
Net margin reached 9.5%, up 324 basis points sequentially and 7.3 percentage points year over year. Sequentially, net income rose while operating income fell.

AMD's gross margin of 50.2% sat above the sector median of 43.4% and below the 75th percentile of 55.2%. Its operating margin of 10.8% compared with a sector median of 3.0% and a 75th percentile of 14.8%.
AMD's year-over-year revenue growth of 35.9% was exceeded by three of the nine listed peers: NVDA at 69.2%, MRVL at 63.3% and MU at 38.3%.
Seven of the nine peers reported higher operating margins than AMD, ranging from MRVL at 14.3% to NVDA at 49.1%. Only INTC and ON were below AMD.
R&D intensity of 23.2% was above the sector median of 19.3% and below the 75th percentile of 25.6%.
The 2024Q1 SG&A figure is flagged as restated or recast, with both values kept, so the year-over-year SG&A comparison should be confirmed against the latest filing.
All 2024Q4 figures are pipeline-derived, likely as annual minus nine-month year-to-date amounts, so every sequential comparison depends on that derivation.
NVIDIA reported 2024Q2 revenue of $30.04 billion, up 15.3% from 2024Q1 and up 122.4% from 2023Q2, while operating income reached $18.64 billion.
Revenue rose from $26.04 billion in 2024Q1 and from $13.51 billion in 2023Q2.
Gross profit was $22.57 billion, up 10.6% sequentially, slower than the 15.3% revenue growth, so gross margin fell 3.2 percentage points to 75.1% from 78.4% in 2024Q1.
Cost of revenue increased to $7.47 billion from $5.64 billion in 2024Q1.
Year over year, gross profit grew 138.6%, faster than revenue's 122.4%, lifting gross margin 5.1 percentage points from 70.1% in 2023Q2.

R&D expense rose to $3.09 billion from $2.72 billion in 2024Q1 and $2.04 billion in 2023Q2, yet R&D as a share of revenue edged down 0.2 percentage points sequentially to 10.3% and fell 4.8 percentage points year over year.
SG&A expense was $842 million, compared with $777 million in 2024Q1 and $622 million in 2023Q2.
Operating income grew 10.2% sequentially, below revenue growth, so operating margin declined 2.9 percentage points to 62.1% from 64.9%.
Against 2023Q2, operating income rose 174.1% and operating margin expanded 11.7 percentage points from 50.3%.
Net income was $16.60 billion, up 11.5% sequentially and 168.2% year over year, giving a net margin of 55.3%, down 1.9 percentage points from 2024Q1 and up 9.4 percentage points from 2023Q2.
NVIDIA's 75.1% gross margin sits well above the sector 75th percentile of 55.3% and the sector median of 45.8%, and above the highest of the nine listed peers, AVGO at 63.9%.
Its 62.1% operating margin compares with a sector median of 4.4%, a sector 75th percentile of 18.2%, and a top peer figure of 32.7% at TXN.
Only four of the nine peers grew revenue year over year, with MU the fastest at 81.5%, still well below NVIDIA's 122.4%.
NVIDIA's R&D intensity of 10.3% is below the sector 25th percentile of 12.3% and the sector median of 19.5%.
NVIDIA reported 2024Q3 revenue of $35.08 billion, up 16.8% from 2024Q2 and up 93.6% from 2023Q3, while operating income rose to $21.87 billion, up 109.9% year over year.
Revenue increased from $30.04 billion in 2024Q2 and from $18.12 billion in 2023Q3 to $35.08 billion in 2024Q3.
Gross profit was $26.16 billion, up 15.9% quarter over quarter, which is slower than the 16.8% revenue growth, so gross margin contracted 0.6 percentage points to 74.6% from 75.1% in 2024Q2.
Year over year, gross profit grew 95.2% against revenue growth of 93.6%, so gross margin expanded 0.6 percentage points from 74.0% in 2023Q3.
R&D expense rose to $3.39 billion from $3.09 billion in 2024Q2 and $2.29 billion in 2023Q3, but as a share of revenue it fell to 9.7% from 10.3% in 2024Q2 and 12.7% in 2023Q3.

R&D intensity declined 0.6 percentage points quarter over quarter and 3.0 percentage points year over year, while SG&A expense rose to $897 million from $842 million in 2024Q2 and $689 million in 2023Q3.

Operating income grew 17.3% quarter over quarter, faster than revenue, lifting operating margin 0.3 percentage points to 62.3% from 62.1% despite the lower gross margin, as operating expenses grew more slowly than revenue.
Year over year, operating margin expanded 4.8 percentage points from 57.5% in 2023Q3.

Net income was $19.31 billion, up 16.3% quarter over quarter and 108.9% year over year; net margin of 55.0% was down 0.2 percentage points from 55.3% in 2024Q2 but up 4.0 percentage points from 51.0% in 2023Q3.
NVIDIA's 74.6% gross margin was well above the sector median of 46.8% and the 75th percentile of 55.4%, and above the highest listed peer, AVGO, at 64.1%.
Its 62.3% operating margin compared with a sector median of 5.0% and a 75th percentile of 19.6%, and exceeded the highest listed peer operating margin, TXN at 37.4%.

NVIDIA's 93.6% year-over-year revenue growth was the highest among the listed companies, narrowly ahead of MU at 93.3% and AVGO at 51.2%, while four of the nine peers (TXN, ADI, ON and INTC) reported year-over-year revenue declines.
NVIDIA's R&D intensity of 9.7% sat below the sector 25th percentile of 11.7% and the median of 20.2%, reflecting its larger revenue base relative to R&D spend.

NVIDIA reported 2024Q4 revenue of $39.33 billion, up 12.1% from 2024Q3 and up 77.9% from 2023Q4, with net income of $22.09 billion; all 2024Q4 and 2023Q4 figures were derived by the pipeline from filings rather than disclosed directly as quarterly values.
Revenue rose from $35.08 billion in 2024Q3 and from $22.10 billion in 2023Q4.
Gross profit was $28.72 billion, up 9.8% quarter over quarter, which lagged the 12.1% revenue increase, so gross margin fell 153 basis points to 73.0% from 74.6% in 2024Q3.
Year over year, gross profit grew 71.1% against revenue growth of 77.9%, so gross margin was down 294 basis points from 76.0% in 2023Q4.
R&D expense was $3.71 billion versus $3.39 billion in 2024Q3, and R&D as a share of revenue eased 22 basis points to 9.4% from 9.7%.
Against 2023Q4, when R&D was $2.465 billion and 11.2% of revenue, R&D intensity was down 171 basis points.
SG&A expense was $975 million, compared with $897 million in 2024Q3 and $712 million in 2023Q4.

Operating income was $24.03 billion, up 9.9% quarter over quarter and 76.5% year over year, and operating margin of 61.1% was down 123 basis points from 62.3% in 2024Q3 and down 49 basis points from 61.6% in 2023Q4.
Net income grew 14.4% quarter over quarter, faster than revenue, so net margin rose 113 basis points to 56.2%; year over year net income grew 79.8% and net margin was up 59 basis points.
NVIDIA's 73.0% gross margin sat well above the sector 75th percentile of 54.7% and the highest peer gross margin of 68.0% at AVGO.
Its 61.1% operating margin compared with a sector median of 6.0% and a 75th percentile of 21.7%, and with AVGO's 42.0%, the highest among the nine peers.
Year-over-year revenue growth of 77.9% exceeded eight of the nine peers, trailing only MU at 84.3%, while four of the nine peers reported revenue declines.
R&D intensity of 9.4% was below the sector 25th percentile of 11.0% and the sector median of 19.2%.
NVIDIA reported 2025Q1 revenue of $44.06 billion, up 69.2% from 2024Q1 and up 12.0% from 2024Q4, but operating income fell 10.0% sequentially to $21.64 billion as operating margin narrowed to 49.1%.
The sequential comparisons rely on 2024Q4 figures derived by the pipeline rather than disclosed directly, including 2024Q4 revenue of $39.33 billion and operating income of $24.03 billion.
Revenue rose from $26.04 billion in 2024Q1 and from $39.33 billion in 2024Q4 to $44.06 billion in 2025Q1.
Cost of revenue rose to $17.39 billion from $10.61 billion in 2024Q4, growing faster than revenue, so gross profit fell 7.2% sequentially to $26.67 billion despite higher revenue.
Gross margin was 60.5%, down 12.5 percentage points from 73.0% in 2024Q4 and down 17.8 percentage points from 78.4% in 2024Q1.
Year over year, gross profit grew 30.7%, well below revenue growth of 69.2%, which is consistent with the gross margin compression.
R&D expense was $3.99 billion versus $3.71 billion in 2024Q4 and $2.72 billion in 2024Q1, while SG&A expense was $1.04 billion versus $975 million in 2024Q4 and $777 million in 2024Q1.
Because R&D grew more slowly than revenue, R&D intensity eased to 9.1% of revenue, down 0.4 percentage points sequentially and down 1.4 percentage points year over year.

Operating margin of 49.1% was down 12.0 percentage points from 2024Q4 and down 15.8 percentage points from 2024Q1, with the decline driven arithmetically by lower gross margin rather than higher operating expense intensity.
Operating income still rose 28.0% year over year, and net income of $18.8 billion was up 26.2% year over year but down 15.0% from 2024Q4.
Net margin was 42.6%, down 13.6 percentage points sequentially and down 14.5 percentage points year over year.
Even after compression, NVIDIA's gross margin of 60.5% sat above the sector 75th percentile of 55.2%, though two of the nine peers, AVGO at 68.0% and ADI at 61.0%, reported higher gross margins.
